components.name: Job Queue
components.quality_responsibility: Lossless job ingestion, persistence, and ordered buffering.
components.local_contribution: Buffers incoming job bursts asynchronously so arrival spikes do not force instant upstream dispatches, holding jobs safely until rate limit capacity is available.

components.name: Rate Limiter
components.quality_responsibility: Strict enforcement of upstream rolling rate limit bounds (<= 100 req / 60s).
components.local_contribution: Paces request dispatches across a rolling 60-second window to guarantee upstream hard limit compliance.

components.name: HTTP Dispatcher
components.quality_responsibility: Reliable 1-to-1 HTTP execution, timeout management, and transport error handling.
components.local_contribution: Executes single HTTP requests for dequeued jobs, managing network transport and connection lifecycles.

components.name: Job Completion Tracker
components.quality_responsibility: Accurate job lifecycle state tracking, metrics accounting, and idempotency control.
components.local_contribution: Records job completion/failure states, preventing duplicate executions and ensuring all 500 jobs/hour are accounted for.

EVIDENCE GAPS / ASSUMPTIONS.detail: No candidate HTTP client implementation code, system architecture diagram, or configuration artifact was supplied for evaluation.
Upstream response latency is bounded (average < 5s), allowing rapid processing of queued jobs well within the 1-hour window.
Jobs are strictly independent and map 1-to-1 to single HTTP requests as stated in the brief.

material_failure_modes: Queue buffer overflow or job dropping during a 500-job initial burst.
Premature job expiration (TTL timeout) while queued during rate-limited processing.
requirements: REQ-Q1: Must buffer at least 500 concurrent job payloads without data loss.
REQ-Q2: Job retention/TTL in queue must be >= 1 hour to survive rate-limited backlog draining.
tests: TEST-Q1: Enqueue 500 jobs simultaneously; verify 100% payload retention and queue depth = 500.
TEST-Q2: Hold 500 jobs in queue for 15 minutes during throttled execution; verify zero jobs expire prematurely.

material_failure_modes: Fixed-window boundary burst violation (e.g., 100 reqs at 00:59 and 100 reqs at 01:01, yielding 200 reqs in 2 minutes across boundary).
Clock drift or race conditions allowing parallel workers to exceed aggregate 100 req/min limit.
requirements: REQ-RL1: Must use a rolling 60-second sliding window or continuous token bucket enforcing strictly <= 100 request tokens per 60,000 ms.
REQ-RL2: Rate limit state must be globally synchronized across all concurrent worker threads/processes.
tests: TEST-RL1: Issue continuous dispatch calls at maximum frequency for 10 minutes; continuously inspect every sliding 60,000 ms interval and verify count <= 100.
TEST-RL2: Run parallel worker threads contending for rate tokens; verify aggregate outbound request rate strictly obeys 100 req/min limit.

material_failure_modes: Unthrottled automatic HTTP retries bypassing the rate limiter and causing upstream limit breaches.
Unbounded HTTP connection/read timeouts causing worker thread starvation and throughput underperformance (< 500 jobs/hour).
requirements: REQ-HD1: Every outbound HTTP request attempt (including retries and redirects) must acquire a fresh token from the Rate Limiter.
REQ-HD2: Outbound HTTP timeouts must be explicitly set (e.g., <= 10s) to guarantee thread availability and overall throughput.
tests: TEST-HD1: Mock upstream 503 responses to trigger retries; verify each retry request consumes a Rate Limiter token and total upstream rate remains <= 100 req/min.
TEST-HD2: Simulate upstream latency of 5s per request; verify system processes all 500 jobs in under 10 minutes.

material_failure_modes: Non-atomic job completion recording leading to duplicate execution and wasted rate limit budget.
Inaccurate throughput reporting masking job completion failures.
requirements: REQ-CT1: Must provide atomic completion status updates and deduplicate job execution IDs.
REQ-CT2: Must emit real-time metrics on completed jobs/hour and active rolling req/min.
tests: TEST-CT1: Simulate process crash after HTTP dispatch but prior to queue ack; verify state reconciliation prevents duplicate upstream HTTP requests.
TEST-CT2: Execute 500 jobs; verify tracker metrics accurately reflect exactly 500 completions and peak rolling rate <= 100 req/min.

interface_handoffs.handoff_failure_mode: Queue pushes a batch of jobs assuming Rate Limiter will buffer them, but Rate Limiter uses fixed-window checks, allowing 100 jobs to cross minute boundaries within a short span.
interface_handoffs.requirement: REQ-INT1: Queue processing must be strictly pull-based or token-gated by the Rate Limiter's sliding-window token availability.
interface_handoffs.test: TEST-INT1: Push 500 jobs to queue; record dispatch timestamps and verify no sliding 60-second window contains > 100 job dispatches.

interface_handoffs.handoff_failure_mode: HTTP Dispatcher performs internal connection retries under a single authorization token, resulting in multiple network calls per token.
interface_handoffs.requirement: REQ-INT2: Dispatcher-to-Limiter interface contract must mandate 1 token per physical network transmission attempt.
interface_handoffs.test: TEST-INT2: Force network drop on first attempt of each request; verify Rate Limiter counts second attempt as a separate request.

interface_handoffs.handoff_failure_mode: HTTP call succeeds (200 OK), but network failure on completion handoff causes queue to re-queue the job, consuming rate capacity on duplicate execution.
interface_handoffs.requirement: REQ-INT3: Job completion acknowledgment and state persistence must be idempotent using unique job identifiers.
interface_handoffs.test: TEST-INT3: Inject handoff failure post-200 OK; verify re-queued job is recognized as completed prior to secondary HTTP dispatch.

NON-BLOCKING IMPROVEMENTS: Implement exponential backoff with jitter on HTTP retries to prevent retry thundering herds.
Implement adaptive rate limiting that dynamically reduces dispatch rate upon receiving HTTP 429 responses (guarding against upstream/downstream clock skew).
Expose Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metrics for queue depth, rate limit utilization, and job completion latency.
WHAT NOT TO SPEND TIME ON: Complex distributed consensus protocols (Raft/Paxos) - a single process or lightweight redis/token-bucket token gate is sufficient for 500 jobs/hour (8.33 req/min average).
Advanced job dependency/DAG graph solvers - the brief specifies jobs are independent.
Payload compression or multi-part streaming optimizations unless mandated by upstream.
